elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience, including during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The added operative sentence permits Company to terminate “this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience” without limiting the right to periods when no Statement of Work is outstanding.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice period is 30 days.
elements.evidence: The added sentence expressly requires thirty (30) days' advance notice.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice must be written.
elements.evidence: The added sentence expressly requires “advance written notice.”

elements.element: Upon Customer's termination for convenience, Vendor must refund prepaid fees.
elements.evidence: The added sentence requires Contractor to “refund any prepaid fees” when Company exercises the added convenience-termination right.

elements.element: The refund of prepaid fees must be calculated pro rata for the period after the effective termination date.
elements.evidence: The refund is expressly required “on a pro rata basis for the period after the effective date of such termination.”

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section (a) continues to permit Contractor to terminate the Agreement for any or no reason whenever no uncompleted Statement of Work is outstanding. That trigger is not expressly limited to the end of the Agreement's committed term, so Contractor could terminate during an Agreement term if no SOW were then outstanding.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience, including during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The added sentence gives Company an unrestricted right to terminate the Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice period is 60–90 days.
elements.evidence: The operative notice period is thirty (30) days, not a period within the stated 60–90-day fallback range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer does not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed for Company's convenience termination; accordingly, there is no fee exceeding the three-month cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Contractor may terminate whenever no uncompleted Statement of Work is outstanding, which is not expressly tied to the end of the Agreement or any defined term.

elements.element: Vendor must give 90 days' notice to terminate for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section (a) permits Contractor to terminate on only fifteen (15) days' advance notice.

result.reason: The redline adds the requested Company convenience-termination right, 30-day written notice, and pro-rata refund, but it does not adequately restrict Contractor's existing convenience right to periods outside every committed term. It also does not meet the fallback's Vendor end-of-term and 90-day-notice restrictions. Because neither complete level is reached, the redline is not minimal for purposes of the rule. Unrelated breach, payment, and work-product provisions remain operative, although the overlapping 15-day and 30-day Company convenience rights and the undefined relationship between “no uncompleted Statement of Work” and a committed Agreement term reduce drafting clarity.
